code-design.note: Accurate unit signatures, numbered call chain with labeled error paths E0-E5, explicit assumptions list and test seams; misses that the repo currently fails to build.

plain.note: Correct verified-current-state section and a smart native-ID PUT that avoids custom-ID params, but includes function bodies, has no error-path table, and misses the broken build.

feature-dev.note: Uniquely catches the real duplicate DetailFormatter.FormatComments that breaks go build, compares three approaches, covers json output, empty list ID and no-status lists, with a commit sequence; scope is broader (debug to stderr, SetBaseURL, cmd.OutOrStdout).

superpowers.note: Concise, accurate (debug Printf line numbers check out) and has a good error table, but the command snippet elides the PUT, it lacks signatures for several units, and it misses the broken build.

reason: Y verified the repository state most deeply and found a real blocker (go build fails because FormatComments is declared twice in internal/output/table.go), then designed the remaining edge cases (empty list ID, empty status list, json output on the already-in-status path) and an ordered commit plan. W is the cleanest and most reviewable design with explicit error paths and assumptions but did not notice the build failure, while X and Z are correct but thinner on failure paths and open decisions.
